style.medium: photorealistic 3D render and photographic texture work, high dynamic range, physically plausible materials, subtle film grain and lens dirt
style.light: late blue hour dusk with warm sodium streetlamps, pulsing cold blue and red police strobe from behind, low warm headlights and greenish shop spill, wet-ground reflections
style.camera: low third-person chase camera just above hip height, slightly wide, shallow atmospheric haze in the distance
style.detail: high micro-detail: puddle sheen, chipped paint, road seams, grit, rain film on glass, worn edges on every man-made surface

elements.name: title_lockup
elements.description: The words STREET ESCAPE in heavy condensed grotesque capitals, stacked on two lines, cut out with a thin cold rim of light along the top edges as if lit by a streetlamp from above, surfaces faintly scuffed and stencilled rather than glossy, nothing behind them
elements.place: centre of the start screen, upper middle, over the street backdrop

frames.alpha: see-through around the subject and through a hole at x 424-804, y 64-520 px

elements.seen: Two rows of heavily distressed dark gray block letters arranged side by side spelling STREET above ESCAPE, facing toward the viewer, with a solid light gray rectangular empty space painted inside the letter C.

elements.name: start_backdrop
elements.description: A single held dusk residential street corner seen from low eye height: wet cracked asphalt with puddle reflections of amber lamps, cracked kerb, one parked hatchback and a van with a blinking hazard light, a lit upstairs window, brick wall with chipped paint, chain-link gate, faint blue-grey overcast sky with a warm smear at the horizon, everything slightly soft in distance haze
elements.place: full bleed behind the start screen and as the page's outside frame
elements.seen: A realistic wet street scene at twilight with a reflective road, buildings, parked vehicles, and a sunset sky, where a gray car and white van on the left face away and empty areas exist in the road and sky.
